narrative.overview:
DEADBOARD looks like a piece of test equipment that tells the truth. Every surface is a
readout or a control: labelled, ruled, exact, with nothing decorative. The board on the bench
is the brightest object on screen. Around it the chrome sits in four green-tinted near-blacks
separated by 1px hairlines, the way a front panel is divided by engraved lines rather than
raised boxes. Values come in monospace with their unit, labels in small uppercase, and
explanations in plain Inter.

Density stays high on every screen size. Controls are compact (28px), text is small but
high-contrast, and the side panel reads like a spec sheet: titled sections, key/value lists,
ruled objective rows. The bench is an operating surface, so the only colour that means "brand"
is Phosphor Green. The ok/warn/danger status colours and the instrument signal colours (probe
red, scope yellow, supply volts green, supply amber, the thermal ramp) mean what they mean on a
real bench and are never decoration. The public pages (homepage, learn pages, docs) share the
same tokens at reading scale: larger mono headlines, 16px body, a faint 32px PCB grid behind the
page.

The personality comes from precision and a few earned details, not ornament: the blinking block
cursor after the wordmark, tabular-figure readouts, a terminal well that prints real output,
level numbers banded like CVSS scores. DEADBOARD must never drift toward gamer RGB and neon
glows, toward cartoon kids' education (mascots, bubbly shapes, confetti), or toward Hollywood
hacker theatre (matrix rain, glitch effects, fake terminals that don't show real data).
keyCharacteristics: Dark and green-tinted, with four tonal steps from back to front and 1px hairlines for structure.
One brand accent, Phosphor Green, used for active state, primary action, focus and the brand signal only.
Two families: JetBrains Mono for the brand, readings, values and headlines; Inter for interface and explanation.
Compact everywhere: 28px controls, 11–13px interface text, instrument density on phones too.
Flat by default; a shadow means the element floats over the board.
Every number carries its unit; estimated values are labelled as estimates.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Phosphor Green is the only brand colour. Use it where something is active, primary, focused or alive. If two things on a screen are green, one of them is probably wrong.

rules.name: The Bench Meaning Rule
rules.body: Instrument and status colours mean what they mean on a real bench. Never use Scope Yellow for emphasis, Danger for a brand moment or Supply Amber as a warning. When colour carries information, add a second cue: a label, a value or a shape.

rules.name: The Unit Rule
rules.body: A value is never shown without its unit, and values are always set in mono with tabular figures so readings don't jitter as they change.

rules.name: The Fold Rule
rules.body: On phones, text is shortened or folded (a short lede, a collapsible card), never just shrunk. 11px is the floor for any text that has to be read.

rules.name: The Spec Sheet Rule
rules.body: Lists of things (instruments, objectives, properties) are ruled rows with a hairline between them, not floating cards. A card is used only when it is something you pick.

rules.name: The Floats-Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this sits over the board". Panels, rows and cards that live in the layout get no shadow; they use a tonal step and a hairline instead.

rules.name: The Drawn-Only Rule
rules.body: The cursor names only what the renderer draws (blobs, jumpers, empty footprints, dull joints). A fault the board does not show is never named; it is found by measuring.

dos: **Do** keep Phosphor Green for active, primary, focused or alive states, and put Phosphor Ink text on it (`#04140a` on `#4be38a`, 11.4:1).
**Do** separate layout regions with a tonal step plus a 1px hairline; save shadows for elements that float over the board.
**Do** set every value in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures, followed by its unit (`3.00 V`, `317 mA`), and name parts and nets exactly (`R7788`, `PP3V3_S5`).
**Do** keep controls compact (28px default, 26px small) on every screen size, give key actions and floating view buttons 44px on touch, and never go below 24px for anything tappable.
**Do** pair colour-coded information with a second cue: the level number with its band name, a pass badge with its label, a probe dot with its net.
**Do** show focus with the 2px Phosphor Green outline on every interactive element, and give every icon-only control a name and every toggle its pressed or selected state.
**Do** stop the cursor blink, the smooth scroll and decorative transitions under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** change tokens only in `src/ui/tokens.css`, which both the bench and the website import, and keep `docs/BRAND.md` in step with it.
donts: **Don't** add glows, neon gradients, RGB lighting or "cyber" HUD chrome. The brand guide already bans glows and gradients on the mark, and the same goes for the interface.
**Don't** use mascots, bubbly shapes, confetti or primary-colour gamification. Successes are short dry lines ("All checks green. The board is alive."), not celebrations.
**Don't** fake hacker theatre: no matrix rain, no glitch effects, no terminals printing output the app didn't produce.
**Don't** put white text on Phosphor Green, or recolour the mark's trace.
**Don't** use instrument colours (Scope Yellow, Supply Amber, Probe Red) as decoration or as general emphasis.
**Don't** use a coloured side stripe as an accent on cards, callouts or rows; use a full 1px border with a tinted fill instead.
**Don't** shrink text to make it fit on phones; shorten it or fold it. On the phone tool strip, a tool is as wide as its label and the strip fades at the edge where more tools scroll in.
**Don't** bind a board shortcut to Tab or Space on a focused control; Tab moves focus, and single-key shortcuts must stay switchable off (Settings → Key shortcuts).
**Don't** wrap ruled lists (instruments, objectives, properties) in floating cards.
